Capacity, usage and shared client guidance

What “new-user slots available” means

The Create account page displays N new-user slots available. N is read from the gateway's current account assignments, not written as a fixed number in the page. A slot is a pre-provisioned pair of private execution environments for one new account. It is not a user's project folder count, app-name allowance or GPU request allowance. Internet access still requires administrator approval.

The count updates every 15 seconds while the page is visible and when returning to the tab. If it cannot refresh, the page shows capacity unavailable. Account creation always rechecks allocation on the server; two people viewing the same last slot cannot both claim it. An assigned slot stays reserved when its account is disabled, preserving private files and history. Increasing the prepared pool is an operator deployment action. Remaining slots do not promise worker health; runtime availability is shown separately in the admin dashboard.

Admin capacity and monitoring

Open Admin overview to see:

View Meaning
New-user slots Remaining slots, assigned/prepared slots and enabled/disabled accounts
Browser sessions Sessions authenticated through the main gateway, split by environment
DSH activity Running DSH agents, queued messages, stored conversations, turns and model steps
Token usage Accumulated input/output tokens and separately labelled recorded/recent decode rates
Runtime coverage Responding/configured private runtimes; incomplete coverage is explicit
Storage Per-user/environment workspace and durable file sizes, local state used/capacity, collection time and partial-scan status
Applications Names, ports, enabled state and one administrator-controlled allowance per account
Managed services Administrator-controlled startup and status when the service supervisor is deployed
Access audit Central access records and projection freshness

Capacity and DSH activity refresh every 15 seconds while the dashboard is visible. Unavailable activity clears the numeric cards instead of displaying old numbers as current. A storage collection older than five minutes is marked; the Refresh button does not run a new storage scan. The operator updates storage observations with scripts/collect_admin_capacity.py. Saved infrastructure/model observations retain their own timestamps.

These rates are DSH conversation measurements, not complete Claude Code/Kilo/ TrueForge usage accounting or instantaneous GPU telemetry. Imported histories can increase accumulated token totals; the recent-rate calculation excludes old imported conversations. Missing measurements display unknown rather than zero.

Platform context in all four clients

The shared platform guide supplies DSH, Claude Code, Kilo and TrueForge with the same platform concepts. It explains private accounts, environments, persistent files, app URLs/ports/limits, notebooks, dependencies and managed inference. The clients do not share conversation memory. Live account/app settings remain authoritative when an administrator changes them.

Use DSH as the main web workspace; choose Web Terminal or JupyterLab on login when needed. DSH remains the default landing page. My apps registers a name and port, while the service-startup controls manage a process separately.

Watch capacity update

Create account shows the remaining new-user slots and refreshes as accounts are assigned. The admin view separates prepared capacity from active usage.

  1. Open Create account and read the current new-user slot count.
  2. Two demonstration accounts are created; the visible count changes from two to one to zero.
  3. A refresh failure replaces the number with an unavailable message, then recovers.
  4. Admin overview shows both assigned slots and the account counts.
